subject: math

objective.text: Solve word problems about length. Use tape diagrams and number sentences.

explanations.title: Tape diagram for how many more
explanations.text: Draw one tape for the length now and one for the length you want. Put a question mark on the part you do not know. Then write a number sentence.

explanations.title: Change yards to inches
explanations.text: Sometimes the problem uses two units. One yard is 36 inches. Change the yard to inches before you find the answer.

explanations.title: Two-step problems
explanations.text: Some problems need two steps. First find a length that is missing. Then answer the question that was asked. Reread the problem to check the question.

explanations.title: Difference in a tape diagram
explanations.text: When a rope is 18 inches shorter, 18 is the difference. It is not the length of the short rope. Put the question mark where the total length is.

explanations.title: Draw the triangle
explanations.text: Draw the shape in the story. Two sides are the same length, so write the same number on both. Label the total and the question mark.

explanations.title: Make a ten to add
explanations.text: To add 42 and 19, take 1 from 42. Give it to 19 to make 20. Then add 41 and 20.

examples.title: The scarf
examples.text: The scarf is 19 inches long now. He wants 36 inches. 19 plus what number equals 36? Count up 1 to 20, then 16 more. He needs 17 more inches.

examples.title: The two ropes
examples.text: One rope is 64 inches. The shorter rope is 18 inches less. 64 minus 18 equals 46. Then 64 plus 46 equals 110. Both ropes are 110 inches.

examples.title: The triangle
examples.text: The sides add up to 96 feet. Two sides are 40 feet each. 40 plus 40 equals 80. 96 minus 80 equals 16. The last side is 16 feet.
